attempts.rationale: I will test a weighted combination using inverse error on the full pool, as the series has a very stable ranking and strong trend, so a selective weighted average should work well.
The series is trend-dominated with stable ranking; a selective combination like a trimmed mean may drop the extreme high-error models (e.g., catboost, rf).
The series is trend dominated with stable rankings; a softmax weighting may better balance models without over‑relying on the best ones.
The diagnosis suggests a selective combination due to stable ranking and strong trend; try a median over the full pool to reduce influence of outlier models.
The series is trend‑dominated with stable rankings, so a selective combination like DBA on the top three models may improve on the current weighted pool4 result.
The series is trend dominated with stable ranking; try a per‑model weight that adapts to error trend across windows – a weighted combination on the full pool using error_trend weights.
Test a selective trimmed‑mean on the stable top‑3 pool to see if trimming improves over dba/weighted.
The series is trend‑dominated with stable rankings; a selective dba over the full pool may capture complementary errors better than the top‑3 dba.
The series is trend‑dominated with stable rankings; a simple mean over the top‑3 models may provide a robust baseline and test if averaging beats DBA.

decision.justification: Selected 'dba on pool4' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.268. Series context: trend strength 0.9734 and seasonal strength 0.0; model ranking is stable across windows (Kendall tau 0.828); 6 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 5.151939663425126e+144.
